claim.quote: Presently available data support the presence of a modulated component of unknown origin, with parameters prima facie compatible with a galactic halo composed of light-mass WIMPs. Unoptimized estimators yield a statistical significance for a modulation of ~2.8 sigma, limited by the short exposure.

name: Search for an Annual Modulation in a P-type Point Contact Germanium Dark Matter Detector
notes: Recorded as an anomaly: 'a modulated component of unknown origin' at ~2.8 sigma; the authors do not claim evidence or discovery.

significance.quote: Unoptimized estimators yield a statistical significance for a modulation of ~2.8 sigma, limited by the short exposure.

summary.plain: Fifteen months of CoGeNT data showed a yearly rise and fall in the low-energy event rate, of unknown origin, that fit light dark matter. The significance was about 2.8 sigma, too low to claim a signal.
summary.technical: 15 months (442 live days of 458, 4 Dec 2009 - 6 Mar 2011) of p-type point-contact germanium data; modulation with unconstrained phase, period and amplitude; ~2.8 sigma with unoptimized estimators.

title: Search for an Annual Modulation in a P-type Point Contact Germanium Dark Matter Detector
why_it_matters: The first indication of annual modulation in a germanium detector, reported alongside the DAMA/LIBRA modulation; later germanium and xenon experiments did not confirm it.
